clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move across the country to buy an apple orchard in March 1952, within the year: June's homesickness and anxiety writing daily to her sister in Millbrook, her distance from Walter as he worked long hours in the trees, Glen's fights at his new school, June kept to her bed for weeks that first winter, Walter's cutoff from his brother Harlan over their father's land money, and rows between Walter and June over money for new trees. By September 1953, June joined the church choir and her letters thinned out, marking where the family settled into the new place.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when a late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan: Walter began drinking heavily, he and Glen blamed each other over the loan, Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank, Glen's son Carl's asthma attacks worsened that winter, and you began wetting the bed in April 1969. By October 1969, Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees, marking where the family's immediate crisis eased.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's loss of his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975: Glen sat out of work most of that year in the truck in the yard for hours, you stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer, Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night while loud fights erupted between Glen and Marian over money at night, Glen's son Carl spent most nights at his girlfriend's house, you kept to your room and distanced from your mother, and Walter began drinking again after six years off it. By March 1976, Glen started driving a delivery truck for the feed store, and by June you were eating again and made the track team, marking where things settled.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into Nora and Hollis's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Hollis's mother Wilma selling her farm and moving into your house in January 1990: you clashed with Wilma over the children's bedtimes and meals, Hollis worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows, Hollis took his mother's side, your son Owen had tantrums at preschool, Wilma took over your daughter Lily's care, you developed eczema flared on both hands, and you and Hollis had rows most nights by November 1990. Your mother Marian drove over twice a week to take your side within months. By June 1991, Wilma took a flat in town, and by August your eczema cleared over the summer, marking where the household settled.
